Deathstalker Vincent was a Forsaken scout sent alongside Deathstalker Adamant to infiltrate Shadowfang Keep. Slain by the mad mage Arugal, his corpse remains inside the stronghold as a grim warning to any who challenge the feral worgen within.

Before the Forsaken could launch a full-scale assault against the beasts holding Shadowfang Keep, intelligence on the fortress's interior was desperately needed. Two operatives from the Deathstalkers, the intelligence arm of the Forsaken, slipped past the barricades: Vincent and Adamant. Their mission ended in disaster. While Adamant was captured and locked away in a dungeon cell, Vincent was dragged directly before Shadowfang's master. Refusing to bend the knee or serve Arugal's dark designs, Vincent was executed on the spot, his body discarded on the stone floor to rot as a testament to the mage's fury.

Arugal used Vincent's demise to issue a scathing declaration to the intruders in his keep. Confronting the captive operative, the mad mage mocked the Forsaken and compared their intrusion to the failed efforts of his former Kirin Tor comrades. Demanding that Vincent surrender his blade and secrets to his master, Arugal struck the scout down when he refused, declaring that Vincent's moldering remains would serve as a warning to anyone foolish enough to trespass in his domain.

Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth.

Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation.

Following the Second War, Deathwing sought to tear down mortal kingdoms from within. Taking the human identity of Lord Daval Prestor, a charismatic noble, he charmed King Terenas Menethil II and the high council of the Alliance of Lordaeron, plotting to install himself on the vacant throne of Alterac. Meanwhile, he aided the Dragonmaw clan at Grim Batol to keep Queen Alexstrasza enslaved while harvesting her clutches. His machinations unraveled when Rhonin destroyed the Demon Soul, restoring the other Aspects' stolen power and enabling them to drive Deathwing away.

In the present year, the mortal kingdoms largely assume Deathwing was destroyed or permanently driven from the world. However, the black dragonflight remains an active scourge across Azeroth. Led by his cunning brood, including his daughter Onyxia and son Nefarian, black drakes manipulate the politics of mortals and terrorize the landscape from mountain lairs. The scars of the black Aspect's ancient treachery run deep, and travelers wandering through craggy wastelands and deep subterranean tunnels still fear the stirring of the Great Dragon.

Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand.
A Crusader on the Kaldorei Frontier

Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine.

Delgren's immediate crusade pits him directly against the Cult of the Dark Strand, a malevolent cabal operating around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. Teaming with the scout Balthule Shadowstrike, Delgren orchestrates strikes into the cult's territory, investigating their dark rituals and sending adventurers to strike down cultists, shatter their summoning focuses, and root out corrupt warlocks who dare traffic with demonic shadow.

Despite his fierce devotion to the Holy Light and zealous nickname, Delgren possesses an unusual perspective on Kalimdor's tangled politics. Much to the annoyance and disdain of his conservative superiors, he took the time to learn Orcish. This rare linguistic skill hints at an unconventional mind—one that seeks to understand the enemies and neighbors sharing this untamed continent rather than relying solely on blind dogma.

Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw.

When the years of labor concluded, the House of Nobles ran up colossal debts through military campaigns and refused to provide the Stonemasons their promised compensation. Enraged, VanCleef demanded restitution, only for the nobles to officially dissolve the guild. Leading a riot, VanCleef took the Stonemasons out of the city; in the chaos his lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and left to languish in the Stockade. Taking advantage of the crown's neglect of the countryside, the Defias drove off Westfall's farmers and claimed its rich gold deposits. Within the depths of Moonbrook's Deadmines, VanCleef oversaw the construction of a massive juggernaut warship, preparing an armed assault against Stormwind itself. While the House of Nobles dismissed the thieves as disorganized brigands, VanCleef forged alliances with river crooks, gnolls, and pirates, turning an embittered labor union into an army poised to crush the monarchy.

High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and a trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Once a prominent spiritual leader among Lordaeron's surviving defenders, his fate became tied to the dark descent of the Scarlet Crusade.

Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor of Highlord Alexandros Mograine, the bearer of the legendary Ashbringer. He stood beside the Highlord when Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien founded the Scarlet Crusade, at first a noble order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

Fairbanks accompanied Alexandros Mograine when the Highlord's eldest son, Renault, led them into a terrible Scourge ambush outside Stratholme. Fairbanks fell early under the press of undead claws, buried beneath piles of rotting corpses. From this horrific vantage, he silently witnessed Renault seize the fallen Ashbringer and plunge it into his own father's heart, corrupting the holy blade with patricide. Surviving the slaughter, Fairbanks clawed his way out from under the dead and returned to the Scarlet Monastery to expose Renault's treachery.

Fairbanks's desperate warnings shattered the remaining defenders of Lordaeron. Those who believed his horrific account abandoned the fanatical order to form the Argent Dawn. Those who remained loyal to Renault and Saidan Dathrohan branded Fairbanks a blasphemer and a lunatic. Fairbanks was quietly executed by the Scarlet Crusade. Rather than granting him a holy burial, the crusaders discarded his body in a hidden chamber behind the Cathedral's altar, where he eventually rose as the very monstrosity they swore to cleanse.
